clue.text: Bloomers ripped off: part of a retiring person's en semble?

definitions.text: part of a retiring person's en semble

indicators.note: something ripped off has been torn apart, so the letters before it come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, and also part of the indicator's surface

explanation.surface: Someone's undergarments are torn off as they get ready for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator is 'off', with 'ripped' doing double duty as part of the fodder; all fourteen letters of BLOOMERS RIPPED rearrange to BEDROOM SLIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retiring for the night wears nightclothes, and a bedroom slipper is one item of that outfit.

clue.text: Tree in Spring?

parts.note: surface reading: a tree putting out new growth in springtime
setter's reading: Herbert Beerbohm Tree, the famous Victorian actor-manager, in the spring of his career

explanation.walkthrough: The capital T on 'Tree' is the giveaway: it is the actor Herbert Beerbohm Tree, and a tree in spring is budding.
explanation.definitionFit: A budding actor is one just starting out, as the young Tree once was; budding is also what trees do in spring.

clue.text: Preliminary sketch shows road raised over a foot

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
taken as written
FT is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: An early plan shows a road built up on an embankment about a foot high.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the reversed road above A and FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a first rough version of a drawing or document, before the finished one.

clue.text: An inedible bit of fruit and a twisted organ pipe …

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of shape, so the letters following it are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of odd discarded items: something you can't eat from a fruit, and a bent pipe from an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing ellipsis leads into the next clue, but this clue is complete on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The pips of an orange are its seeds, which are bitter and not eaten.

clue.text: … from among relics of doubtful ancestry

indicators.note: taken from means drawn out of the words that follow, which hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the odd items come from a pile of relics whose origins are uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the clue before, but the hidden letters run through 'among relics'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is a dog of mixed or unknown breeding, so its ancestry is doubtful.

clue.text: A relatively insubstantial fireraiser?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: comparative of light, weighing less
second meaning: a device for starting a flame

explanation.surface: An arsonist who is not very substantial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fireraiser' suggests an arsonist; the question mark admits it is only a gadget that raises a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighter is both the comparative of light, meaning less heavy, and the name of a device for igniting cigarettes.

clue.text: The courtyard is quiet at ten

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quiet
taken as written
ten is written 10, which looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: By ten o'clock at night the courtyard has gone silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At ten' reads as a time, but 10 is used as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area or inner courtyard of a house.

clue.text: Add detail to a note sup porting Oriental work in the United States

parts.note: E is east
the American spelling of labour
taken as written
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note is added to support an Eastern work performed in America.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue A TE sits below, 'supporting', the rest; the printed 'sup porting' is a line break in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to develop something by filling in more detail.

clue.text: Lawyer without force or emotion

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside, so the lawyer's letters sit around the other piece

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
to ram is to force something in

explanation.surface: A lawyer delivers a speech that is flat, with neither force nor feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside'; DA is an American district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama in everyday speech is heightened emotional excitement or fuss, as in 'don't make a drama of it'.

clue.text: Drink going to the head late on?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an alcoholic drink taken before bed

definitions.text: going to the head late on?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cap worn on the head at night

explanation.surface: Alcohol that goes to your head late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to the head' sounds like alcohol's effect, but the second reading is literal: headwear put on late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is both a bedtime alcoholic drink and the old-fashioned cloth cap worn in bed.

clue.text: To sit in Tunis is to change customs

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters before it are altered into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking a seat in the Tunisian capital means adapting to local habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says a visitor to Tunis must change their customs; 'change' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution can be an established custom or practice, such as the institution of marriage.

clue.text: Number one regent deposed

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a deposed ruler is overthrown, so the letters of the ruler are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The top-ranking regent has been removed from power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like a single phrase meaning the top person; split it, and 'Number' is the definition while 'one' joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, so it is a kind of number.

clue.text: Lampblack applied wrong way to balloon: spherical shape lost immoderately early

indicators.note: put on the wrong way round, so the letters for lampblack run backwards

parts.note: lampblack is the fine black soot from lamps

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so the named shape is taken out of the word for the balloon

parts.note: taken as written
a ball is a sphere

explanation.surface: Someone smears soot on a balloon the wrong way, and it loses its round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: SOOT reversed gives TOOS; BALLOON without BALL leaves OON.
explanation.definitionFit: Too soon means before the right moment, which is exactly what immoderately early describes.

clue.text: Dance of the old convict going back to work

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the convict's word is read right to left

parts.note: an old lag is a hardened prisoner
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A dance performed by an ex-prisoner who is returning to his job.
explanation.walkthrough: Old lag is British slang for a long-serving convict, and OP (opus) is the usual crossword abbreviation for a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: The galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in quick duple time.

clue.text: Listen and learn in slap dash fashion about English

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation
slapdash means careless and haphazard, so the letters are set down in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Pay attention and pick up English haphazardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen and learn' looks like one instruction, but only 'Listen' is the definition; 'and' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom for paying attention to someone, which is to listen.

clue.text: Big shed wanted for epic film

parts.note: large means big
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: A huge shed is needed as a set for a big screen epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' wants to be a garden building, but it is the verb: a snake sheds or casts its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic films traditionally need hundreds of actors and extras, so a big cast is what such a production requires.

clue.text: Dance movement excludes one from the whole conversation

indicators.note: to exclude is to leave something out, so a numeral drops out of the following word

parts.note: entire means whole
I is the Roman numeral one
a chat is a conversation

explanation.surface: A dancer's routine leaves one person out of the whole discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance movement' could suggest a political movement in the surface, but it is the ballet step being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet leap in which the dancer crosses the legs repeatedly in the air.

clue.text: Plotted in study built like church

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over
a church typically has a spire

explanation.surface: A scheme was hatched inside a study designed to look like a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plan secretly together, so plotted is a direct synonym of the past tense.

clue.text: He tells the truth about a table

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a table of items is a list

explanation.surface: An honest man reports the facts about a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container or reversal signal, but here it is simply RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist faces facts and describes things as they actually are, so he tells the truth.

clue.text: One who wants Teacher to cut the grass standing up

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, so the teacher goes inside the grass
in a down clue, standing up means the word reads upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
schoolchildren call a male teacher sir

explanation.surface: Someone wants the teacher to mow the tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests mowing, but here it means slicing into the reversed grass; sir is what pupils call a male teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To desire is to want, so a desirer is a person who wants something.

clue.text: River gold extracted from flood

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out, so the precious metal leaves the larger word

parts.note: a torrent is a flood of water
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Gold is panned out of the floodwater of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: TORRENT loses OR to leave TRENT, a major river of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is one of the longest rivers in England, flowing through Nottingham to the Humber.

clue.text: Instrument played con aria agitato?

indicators.note: music that is played is performed freely, so the letters that follow are performed in a new order
agitato is a musical direction meaning agitated, and agitated letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aria is performed with agitation on some instrument, as an Italian score might direct.
explanation.walkthrough: Italian 'con' and 'agitato' make the clue look like a musical score, but CON ARIA is just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: All over a wedding cake?

parts.note: surface reading: the wedding has ended, or something is spread everywhere
setter's reading: the sugary coating that covers the whole cake

explanation.walkthrough: 'All over' suggests finished, but it means literally covering every surface of the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding cake is traditionally coated entirely in a hard white sugar layer.

clue.text: Maybe he's right to gamble and drink

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word could be otherwise, so its letters are rearranged into another possibility

parts.note: the letters of he's
R is the abbreviation for right
to bet is to gamble

explanation.surface: A man perhaps has the right to have a flutter and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe he's right' reads as doubting someone; 'Maybe' actually turns HES into SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is a sweet fizzy drink, and in Australian slang a sherbet is a beer.

clue.text: Beauty is beastly at first to a Frenchwoman

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of beastly
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A nod to Beauty and the Beast: the beauty treats a French girl badly at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Beauty and the Beast, which is a French tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired at an event.

clue.text: Poet loses point, he confirms

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so one letter drops out of the poet's word

parts.note: a versifier writes verse
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A poet misses the point, and someone backs that up.
explanation.walkthrough: VERSIFIER without S leaves VERIFIER.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify is to confirm something is true, so a verifier is one who confirms.

clue.text: He will shortly ring. Your reply?

parts.note: he will contracted is he'll
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone will phone soon; how will you answer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon', but it signals the contraction he'll.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the usual greeting given when answering a ringing telephone.

clue.text: Early risers include that lady in Brigworth St perhaps

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in, so the woman's word goes inside the street name
perhaps marks the street name as only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: an invented street name, taken letter by letter
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: People who get up early live on a street called Brigworth St, with a certain woman among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early risers' sounds like people up at dawn; the risers are pioneers of powered flight, who rose into the air early in aviation history.
explanation.definitionFit: Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first powered aeroplane flights in 1903, so they were among the earliest to rise by machine.
